# Finding the Antiderivative of -3*exp(x)*cos(x)

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I need to evaluate ∫ -3*exp(x)*cos(x) dx.

First, let me find I = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx using integration by parts twice.

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) \, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (for ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) \, dx = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) \, dx = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

$$I = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x) \cdot (\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Final Result

Multiplying by -3:

$$\int -3 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) \, dx = -\frac{3}{2} \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot (\cos(x) + \sin(x)) + C$$

**Verification:** Differentiating $-\frac{3}{2} \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot (\cos(x) + \sin(x))$:

$$= -\frac{3}{2} \cdot \left[\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x)) + \text{exp}(x)(-\sin(x)+\cos(x))\right]$$

$$= -\frac{3}{2} \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot 2\cos(x) = -3 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>-3/2*exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + C</answer>
